title: Alpha Just Crossed ₹50 Crore. It Might Still Be the Film That Killed the Spy Universe.
excerpt: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari's action thriller hits a milestone that masks a massive commercial loss — and the YRF Spy Universe's third consecutive stumble.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Alpha crossed ₹50 crore but is projected to incur significant losses.
  • YRF Spy Universe faces three consecutive failures with Alpha, Tiger 3, and War 2.
  • Sharvari achieves her third film crossing ₹50 crore, showcasing her rising stardom.
  • Alpha's overseas gross of ₹24 crore falls short of expectations for the franchise.
  • The Spy Universe needs a creative overhaul to regain audience interest.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=nkrqSW1UOKI The number looks fine on paper. **Alpha**, the latest entry in the **YRF Spy Universe**, has crossed the ₹50 crore net mark at the Indian box office — Day 8, roughly ₹50.05 crore, with a worldwide gross of around ₹83 crore. For a female-led action film in India, that's not nothing. But let's not pretend this is a win. Alpha was made on a reported budget of **₹100 crore**. At its current trajectory — projections land it between ₹55 and ₹65 crore lifetime India net — the film will return less than two-thirds of what it cost to make. Add prints, advertising, and the distributor's cut, and **Yash Raj Films is looking at a substantial commercial loss**. A third one in a row from the Spy Universe, after the limp runs of *Tiger 3* and the outright disaster of *War 2*. > "The fact that this film, with everything going against it, has managed to get off the ground is a minor positive. Ultimately, it's about money rather than positives, and money this film will lose, heavily." That's not a critic. That's a trade analyst summarising the situation with clinical accuracy. ## The Spy Universe Has a Problem > **"Ultimately, it's about money rather than positives, and money this film will lose, heavily." That's not a critic."** **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari** were supposed to inject new energy into a franchise that had grown stale. The trailer promised slick action choreography, a globetrotting aesthetic, and two women doing what Hrithik, Salman, and Shah Rukh had done before them. The audience showed up on opening day — ₹9.50 crore isn't bad for a Friday — but the word of mouth couldn't sustain the momentum. By the weekdays, Alpha was collecting in the ₹2-3 crore range, bleeding screens and losing ground. Then **Dhamaal 4** arrived on July 10 and ate its lunch. Alpha's screen count dropped from 7,000+ to 4,800 overnight. Morning occupancies fell to 6%. By the time the first Saturday of its second week rolled around, the film was collecting ₹1.50 crore — an 85% drop from its opening Friday. The pattern is now undeniable. *Tiger 3* disappointed. *War 2* disappointed harder. Alpha has followed suit. Three consecutive entries in the **YRF Spy Universe** have failed to justify their budgets, and the question has shifted from "can this franchise grow?" to "should it continue at all?" ![Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d6/YRF_Spy_Universe_logo.jpg) ## Sharvari's Quiet Milestone Here's the thing about Alpha's ₹50 crore mark — it belongs to **Sharvari** as much as it does to Alia. This is her third consecutive film to cross the half-century: *Munjya* and *Main Vaapas Aaunga* did it before, and both were made at a fraction of Alpha's cost. She's building something real. Not through headline-grabbing social media moments or controversy, but through steady, solid choices and screen presence that holds up against one of Bollywood's biggest stars. At 28, she's quietly becoming one of the most bankable actors in Hindi cinema — the kind you can build a ₹20-30 crore film around and actually make money. The irony is thick: Alpha may fail as a commercial enterprise, but it might end up being the film that confirmed **Sharvari** as a bona fide star.

## What This Means for NRI Audiences The Spy Universe always played well internationally — the globetrotting action, the premium production values, the escapist fantasy of Indian agents saving the world. **Alpha's overseas gross stands at around ₹24 crore**, which is decent but nowhere near the ₹40-50 crore that a healthy Spy Universe film should be pulling. The diaspora showed up for the opening weekend and largely moved on. For NRI audiences who grew up on *Ek Tha Tiger* and *War*, the decline stings. These were the films you could take your non-Indian friends to and feel proud of the production quality. Now, the franchise needs a serious creative overhaul before it can reclaim that space. ## Where Does YRF Go From Here? **Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan 2** is reportedly in development, and that might be the reset the universe needs. SRK's post-comeback aura is still potent enough to carry a spectacle. But the days of launching new characters with ₹100 crore budgets and hoping the Spy Universe brand alone will sell tickets? Those days are over.
Sharvari's Rising Star Power

Alpha proved that a recognisable franchise badge and two talented leads are not enough. You need a story that earns the audience's excitement, not one that assumes it. The ₹50 crore milestone is real. So is the loss. Both deserve to be acknowledged.
